paragraphs: Rav Natan, father of Rav Huna son of Rav Natan.

Hyman says that he was identified through his son because his son was better known and more famous as the Exilarch in Rav Ashi’s time. Similarly, in the reading Hyman attributes to Dikdukei Soferim, [Chagigah 5b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.5b.21) has Rav Idi, father of Rabbi Yaakov [supplied ר״י] bar Idi. [Shabbat 56b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.56b.18) has Abba, father of R’ Yirmeyah bar Abba, and there are other examples. Hyman says that this Rav Natan was himself a great one of the generation. In his account of [Pesachim 117b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.117b.17), Natan recited Kiddush before Rav Papa in the manner of the elders of Pumbedita, and Rav Papa praised him. Hyman says that [the Rif on Yoma 6b](https://www.sefaria.org/Rif_Yoma.6b.1) and Dikdukei Soferim give a corresponding reading at [Yoma 87b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.87b.11). In [Pesachim 43b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.43b.5) Natan raises an objection, and in [Zevachim 70b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.70b.8) he challenges a teaching.[^4]

notes.text: The R-Y in the Rav Idi example remains unresolved. The checked Pesachim passage explicitly names Rav Papa and the Pumbedita formula. The son’s office and explanation of the father’s appellation are Hyman’s statements.

The whole saved Davidson Chagigah 5b scalar 20 explicitly reads Rav Idi, father of Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi. This supplies the local R-Y expansion, without a new inspection of Dikdukei Soferim or proving that work’s exact variant. The father is Rav Natan; the son is Rav Huna son of Rav Natan, not another generation. Hyman owns the Exilarch office, date, appellation explanation and great-of-the-generation characterization. The Pumbedita phrase means in the elders’ manner, not physically in front of them; Papa’s name comes from the earlier consultation, not a freshly read Pesachim scalar. Yirmeyah’s uninspected abbreviated title remains R-prime, as does Papa’s. All explicit full Rav titles remain.

The consulted Chagigah 5b spells out Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi. Shabbat 56b names Abba and also gives his brother Acha as an alternative. In Pesachim 117b, Rav Natan leads the service before Rav Papa and recites according to the elders of Pumbedita. The discussion concerns the formula for both prayer and Kiddush. The consulted Vilna text of Rif Yoma 6b–7a identifies the service there as Ne’ilah and includes Rav Natan leading it before Rav Papa, who praises him. In the consulted Bavli Yoma 87b, Ulla leads before Rava and is praised, then Rav Huna son of Rav Natan speaks about an individual’s confession. The Dikdukei Soferim reading is cited on Hyman’s authority. The directly consulted Pesachim 43b and Zevachim 70b preserve the objection and challenge with slightly different forms of Huna’s patronymic.

Pesachim has Rav Natan lead the service before Rav Papa. The linked Rif likewise names Natan and Papa in the discussion of Ne’ilah. The Bavli in Yoma gives Ulla leading before Rava, then quotes Rav Huna son of Natan about confession. Those are distinct readings.
